complexity.notes: Compared to the previous submission this just drops a debug print and renames the loop variable. Each recursive level re-squares from scratch, so the total number of multiplications is (L-1)+(L-2)+... = O((log n)^2); ||a single loop that squares a running base while scanning the bits of n (classic binary exponentiation)|| needs only O(log n) multiplications. Turning the recursion into iteration would also cut the O(log n) call stack to O(1) space. The (log n)^2 runtime isn't representable in the benchmark grammar, so 'log n' is given as the nearest polylogarithmic form.
complexity.summary: Recursive exponentiation that peels off the highest set bit of n: it squares x repeatedly to build x^(2^k), then multiplies by the recursive result for the remaining exponent n - 2^k. Negative n is handled by recursing on 1/x with -n.
